==Problem==

What is the minimum possible product of three different numbers of the set <imath>\{-8,-6,-4,0,3,5,7\}</imath>?

<imath>\text{(A)}\ {-336} \qquad \text{(B)}\ {-280} \qquad \text{(C)}\ {-210} \qquad \text{(D)}\ {-192} \qquad \text{(E)}\ 0</imath>

==Solution==

If the product of <imath>3</imath> selected numbers is negative, either all <imath>3</imath> numbers are negative or <imath>1</imath> number is negative and <imath>2</imath> numbers are positive.

The minimum product of <imath>3</imath> negative numbers from this set is <imath>(-8)(-6)(-4) = -192</imath>, while the minimum product of <imath>1</imath> negative number and <imath>2</imath> positive numbers from this set is <imath>(-8)(5)(7) = -280</imath>.

Therefore, the minimum product of <imath>3</imath> numbers from this set is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ {-280}}</imath>.
